content:
When Apple finally responded to the sharp rise in memory and other component costs, it pulled no punches. Some price increases exceeded fifty percent, and pricing for some memory and storage upgrade options even doubled.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come back down...

9to5Mac readers have long questioned whether Apple will lower prices once component supply pressures ease. Over two-thirds of readers indicated they expect these price hikes to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing will not improve until 2028, and even then, any improvement will be quite limited. Prices currently at elevated levels will remain so for at least several years, and will most likely never return to previous levels — a conclusion that now seems self-evident.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Or would you reduce the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Alternatively, would you take other measures such as buying a cheaper model, choosing a refurbished unit, or waiting for a price drop before making a move?

Feel free to take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll allows multiple selections so you can plan to change your purchasing behaviour in multiple ways.
